units: <cite ref="Megillah 15b:17">Meg. 15ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Esther 5:11">Esth. V, 11</cite>) <he>וכמה ר׳ בניו</he> how large was the multitude of his sons? <cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 6:8">Bekh. VI, 8</cite> <he>ר׳ המדבר וכ׳</he> the larger portion of the anterior part of the tongue.

<cite ref="Ketubot 15a:5">Keth. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>הולכין אחר ר׳ העיר</he> we are guided by the legal status of the majority of the inhabitants of the town; <he>ר׳ סיעה</he> the majority of the members of the caravan that encamped near the town.
Ib.; Ḥull. 95ᵃ, a. e. בנמצא הלך אחר הר׳ when a piece of meat is found, we go by the majority of the meat stalls (to decide whether it be kasher or not).
<cite ref="Chullin 3b:14">Ib. 3ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>ר׳ מצויין וכ׳</he> most of those engaged in slaughtering are experts.
<cite ref="Shabbat 118b:7">Sabb. 118ᵇ</cite> <he>רוּבָּן של צדיקים וכ׳</he> most righteous men die from bowel diseases.

<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 2:1">Ḥull. II, 1</cite> <he>רוּבּוֹ של אחד כמוהו</he> if one cuts through the larger portion of the organ (v. <cite ref="O00710"><he>סִימָן</he></cite>), it is considered as if he had cut it through.

<cite ref="Horayot 3b:6">Hor. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>בכל התורה … רובו ככולו</he> in the entire Law we adopt the rule that a majority (or the larger portion) are legally equal to an entirety; <cite ref="Nazir 42a:2">Naz. 42ᵃ</cite>; a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Gittin 60b:2">Gitt. 60ᵇ</cite> <he>ר׳ בכתב וכ׳</he> the majority of the halakhic decisions rests on the Scripture (is derived from the text by interpretation), and the minority on tradition; v. Y. Peah I, 17ᵃ bot.—[<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 4:11:8">Y. Yeb. IV, 6ᵇ</cite> top <he>עד שיפרש לו רובו</he>, read: <he>רַבּוֹ</he>.]
